subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 10-month-old boy is brought for a routine visit because his mother has noticed that his legs are becoming bow-shaped and that he is slow to pull to stand. He was exclusively breastfed until 9 months of age and has never received vitamin D supplementation, and the family lives in a northern city with little sun exposure. Examination shows widened wrists and ankles and palpable beading at the costochondral junctions. Radiographs show cupped, frayed metaphyses.
question: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

options.text: Nutritional rickets due to vitamin D deficiency

explanation_correct: Vitamin D increases intestinal absorption of calcium and phosphate and permits normal mineralization of osteoid. In an exclusively breastfed infant without supplementation or sun exposure, deficiency lowers serum calcium, driving secondary hyperparathyroidism with phosphaturia and hypophosphatemia, so growth-plate cartilage fails to mineralize and produces bowing, metaphyseal widening, and rachitic rosary.

explanation_incorrect.A: Scurvy reflects vitamin C deficiency with defective collagen hydroxylation and produces bleeding gums, perifollicular hemorrhage, and subperiosteal hemorrhage, not widened growth plates.
explanation_incorrect.B: Osteogenesis imperfecta is a type I collagen defect causing recurrent fractures, blue sclerae, and osteopenia beginning at birth, without the rachitic metaphyseal changes.
explanation_incorrect.C: Achondroplasia is an autosomal dominant FGFR3 disorder causing short limbs and frontal bossing from birth with normal calcium, phosphate, and alkaline phosphatase.
explanation_incorrect.D: X-linked hypophosphatemic rickets is caused by FGF23 excess with normal or mildly low calcium, severe hypophosphatemia, and a positive family history; this infant's feeding history and lack of supplementation point to nutritional deficiency.

educationalObjective: Exclusively breastfed infants require vitamin D supplementation because deficiency causes hypocalcemia with secondary hyperparathyroidism and impaired bone mineralization (rickets).
